subject: Post-call recap: Eversafe security & retention fit — evidence path and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Simon <alex.simon@eversafe.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Eversafe security & retention fit — evidence path and next steps

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, your priorities, and proposed next steps so your security team has a single source of truth. If I've missed anything, please flag it.

Key pain points and acceptance criteria you shared:
- Audit logging: need event-level logs (user, request-id, model used, prompt hash, response id, IP, timestamp) for 7+ years for regulatory and investigation purposes.
- Data residency & DPA: EU data must remain in EU regions; you require a DPA with clear retention language and ability to export logs on-demand.
- Evidence for SOC 2 / pen test: need SOC 2 Type II summary and redacted pen test artifacts or a summary from our auditor.
- Ability to run a scoped pen test or provide a vendor-acceptable report and a mechanism to review remediation timelines.
- Production pilot target: governance sign-off by end of Q3 to start a pilot in our EU region (minimum Dedicated pool or Private VPC).

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Configurable retention windows per-customer, with exportable audit logs (CSV/Parquet) and hourly export capability.
- SOC 2 Type II summary and a secure artifact portal for redacted reports under NDA.
- Redacted pen-test executive summary attached; full report available under NDA/audit agreement.
- Key management: we support customer-held keys (KMS/HSM) in Dedicated/Private deployments for EU residency and key separation.
- Deployment options: Hosted EU region with data residency controls; Dedicated pools with SLA; Private VPC for on-prem-like isolation.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Security evidence drop — we will upload SOC2 summary, audit-log sample, retention matrix, and redacted pen-test exec summary to a secured Drive folder by EOD 2027-06-10. (Owner: Marissa)
2) NDA / Audit agreement — Alex to circulate NDA or approve our standard audit access doc so we can share full artifacts. Target: 2027-06-15. (Owner: Alex)
3) Logistics call (technical deep-dive) — schedule 45-min follow-up with Eversafe infra + Redwood security to review log schema, retention APIs, and KMS options. Proposed slots: 2027-06-16 09:00-12:00 UTC or 2027-06-18 13:00-16:00 UTC. (Owner: Irene)
4) Pilot scope & acceptance criteria — draft a short MAP (mutual action plan) for pilot criteria, SLA, and evidence gating by 2027-06-25. (Owner: Jordan)

Attachments in this email: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary, 2p), audit-log-sample.csv, retention-matrix.xlsx.

If that timeline looks reasonable we'll proceed with the evidence upload and lock a follow-up time.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

----
Note: This message contains high-level summaries only. Full artifacts will be shared via our secure artifact portal after NDA/audit agreement.

From: Alex Simon <alex.simon@eversafe.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@eversafe.com
Date: 2027-06-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Eversafe security & retention fit — evidence path and next steps

Irene — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications before we loop legal and infosec: 

1) Audit log detail: can you confirm the log schema includes a request payload hash (we need immutability for prompt content) and model identifier (we must know which model and quantization was used)? The sample CSV will help, but I need to confirm field names for our SIEM mapping.
2) Pen test: the exec summary is helpful — for procurement we typically need either a full redacted report or an auditor attestation (e.g., "no critical findings" letter). What is Redwood's standard route for sharing the full report?
3) Data residency: is customer KMS supported in the Hosted EU region or only in Private/Dedicated? We prefer customer-managed keys in any hosted offering if possible.

We will aim to review the artifacts quickly. Security's initial target for a gating decision is 2027-06-25 (internal review). If we get artifacts and schedule the technical deep-dive this week, that should keep us on track.

Also, please include any expected SLA numbers for Dedicated (p99 latency, throughput guarantees) in the MAP — that'll help procurement.

Alex
Alex Simon
Head of Infrastructure Security
Eversafe Financial
alex.simon@eversafe.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T18:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: Eversafe security & retention fit — evidence path and next steps

Irene / Jordan — adding a few data points to answer Alex's questions and to prepare the artifact drop. Forwarding the recap for context.

Quick answers: 
- Audit log schema: our export includes the following canonical fields: event_ts, request_id, actor_id (internal user id), actor_email, src_ip, model_id, model_variant, prompt_hash (sha256), response_id, token_count, latency_ms, request_payload_size_bytes. I'll attach a 100-line CSV sample (audit-log-sample.csv) for their SIEM mapping.
- Prompt immutability: prompt_hash provides a stable fingerprint; we can also include full prompt text in exports under stricter access controls (portal + NDA).
- SOC 2: we can share a SOC 2 Type II summary today and the redacted report under NDA. We use an external auditor; summary attached (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).
- Pen test: attached is the redacted executive summary (redacted-pen-test-exec-summary.pdf). Full redacted report is available via our secure artifact portal under NDA; we do not send raw pen-test binaries.
- KMS: customer-managed keys are supported in Dedicated and Private deployments today; Hosted EU with customer KMS is in limited preview — we can enable it for pilots under a contract addendum (timeline ~2–3 weeks to enable with legal/ops).
- SLA / Dedicated: Jordan, see below for a short SLA block you can include in the MAP: 99.95% uptime, p99 token latency target measured on our benchmarked profile (model-dependent), burst capacity options, and capacity reservation for pilot sizing. We will provide exact numbers in the MAP.

Planned artifact delivery: I'll upload the files to the Drive folder linked in the thread and share via HubSpot secure attachment. I'll also drop a redaction checklist for the pen-test so procurement knows what to expect.

Recommended next call: Technical deep-dive with Eversafe infra + our platform eng (45 min). Jordan / Irene, please propose 2 slots and I'll include our SRE.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, audit-log-sample.csv, retention-matrix.xlsx, redacted-pen-test-exec-summary.pdf

Marissa Cole
Senior Security PM — Redwood Inference
